label: transparent post-failure methodological amendment
status: PROPOSED -- not yet frozen or applied; requires review before any Exp10 rerun
written_after: Experiment 10 Attempt 1 failed the HotpotQA R4 control-reproduction gate (the second identical-config HotpotQA control failure, after Experiment 9 Attempt 1)
motivation: repeated identical-config control instability: the canonical rabit2 config, with identical dataset selection, prompts, generation settings and logical storage, produced HotpotQA F1 55.2 in 5 runs and 57.7 in 2 runs, entirely from one example's greedy answer ('2016-17' vs '2016–17'); the aggregate +/-1.0 F1 gate cannot absorb a single-example change on a 20-example benchmark (one example = up to 5.0 points)
evidence: results/mlsys2027/control_reproducibility_audit/qa_control_audit.json (read-only; generated by benchmarks/mlsys2027/audit_qa_control_reproducibility.py from committed logs of identical-config bf16 and rabit2 control rows only)
does_not_change: any previously accepted experiment (Exp1-9 accepted evidence untouched)
the status of Exp9 Attempt 1 or Exp10 Attempt 1 (both remain invalid_control_reproduction and excluded)
the LongBench scorer, answer strings (no normalisation), generation settings, datasets, sample selection, configs, logical accounting
the reported scientific metric (official LongBench F1, aggregate mean x 100)
the continuation_ppl, NIAH and passage-retrieval control gates (original tolerances)

audit_basis.reference: the frozen canonical run results/quality/<benchmark>.log (unchanged; it is also the source of the pinned aggregate targets)
limitations: few identical-config runs (7 HotpotQA, 5 Qasper including the reference); the maximum is an empirical observation, not a statistical bound

the canonical reference is itself a single run and is the minority answer on some unstable examples (HotpotQA bf16 index 3, Qasper bf16 index 7); it is kept unchanged because it defines the accepted targets
two runs executed on an NVIDIA H200 instead of an H100 (Exp1 HotpotQA, Exp7 Qasper); their mismatch counts (0-1) are within the H100 range, so no GPU-specific effect is asserted

proposed_rule.scope: generated-QA F1 benchmarks (hotpotqa, qasper); applied identically to the bf16 row and the canonical control row

primary_gate_per_example.definition: a per-example score mismatch is an example whose printed LongBench qa_f1_score differs from the frozen canonical reference run's score for the same dataset index (exact comparison of the logged 3-decimal scores); answer-text differences with an identical score are NOT mismatches but are recorded
primary_gate_per_example.threshold: at most 2 per-example score mismatches per control row per benchmark
primary_gate_per_example.justification: 2 = the maximum observed in any identical-config control run across both benchmarks and both control rows (Qasper rabit2, Exp1); every accepted identical-config run satisfies it
primary_gate_per_example.also_required: the control row's per-example dataset indices equal the reference's (exact sample selection)

proposed_rule.replaces: the aggregate +/-1.0-point F1 control gate for hotpotqa and qasper only

secondary_check_aggregate_envelope.definition: report whether the control's aggregate F1 lies within the historical identical-config envelope above; a value outside the envelope while the primary gate passes is flagged in the report for review
secondary_check_aggregate_envelope.reason_not_hard_gate: with 4-6 comparison runs the envelope is not a reliable bound; a hard envelope would fail on the next new single-example variant exactly as the aggregate gate did

unchanged_mandatory_gates: exact config equality of the control with canonical rabit2
exact dataset / sample selection and per-method counts
original tolerances for continuation_ppl PPL, NIAH and passage-retrieval accuracy, and all logical KV MB checks
